title: Can Deregulation Drive Services Spending?
gist: China is rotating its demand-support effort away from two years of goods-purchase subsidies — whose near-term pull on autos and appliances is now exhausted — toward services consumption, with a flurry of recent government documents and the Politburo's midyear economic meeting explicitly pushing officials to lift services spending. This is a paywall teaser: the title's deregulation angle is never actually developed in the available text, which only sets up the goods-to-services policy pivot.

insights.claim: Chinese households' near-term demand for autos, appliances and other subsidy-eligible goods has been exhausted after two years of high-level policies subsidizing consumer goods purchases, removing the runway for further goods-side stimulus.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Expect fading incremental demand for Chinese autos and white goods as pull-forward reverses; fade names whose 2024-25 volumes leaned on trade-in subsidy programs.
insights.quote: households’ near-term demand for autos, appliances and other subsidized goods has now been exhausted
insights.locator: After two years of high-level policies

insights.claim: China's policymakers are shifting the focus of domestic demand support from subsidized goods purchases to services consumption, marking a change in the channel through which stimulus reaches households.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Rotate China consumer exposure from durable-goods manufacturers toward services beneficiaries (travel, dining, entertainment, healthcare) as policy support follows the new channel.
insights.quote: China’s policymakers are shifting their focus to services
insights.locator: After two years of high-level policies

insights.claim: Services are a more promising target than goods for Chinese demand policy because services consumption is on a structural upward trend, not merely a cyclical or subsidy-driven one.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat the services tilt as a multi-year structural allocation rather than a one-off stimulus trade, since the underlying consumption shift persists beyond any single policy package.
insights.quote: the structural rise in services consumption makes them a more promising target
insights.locator: The government is thus pursuing new avenues

insights.claim: A flurry of recent Chinese government documents has pledged to lift services spending, and the Politburo's midyear meeting on the economy instructed officials to "tap the potential of services consumption" — an explicit top-level mandate rather than a technocratic aside.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Top-level Politburo language is the usual precursor to concrete local implementation measures — watch for follow-through documents naming specific services sectors and funding.
insights.quote: called on officials to “tap the potential of services consumption.”
insights.locator: A flurry of recent government documents
